subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

This is going to be overwhelming for you as you have __taken on work beyond your capabilities.__

options.text: bitten off more than you can chew

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"bitten off more than you can chew"** means taking on more responsibility or tasks than one can manage. (अपनी क्षमता से अधिक काम लेना)

 
 
• **Example:** By agreeing to organize the school festival, she has definitely bitten off more than she can chew.
 
 
 
• **"Overwhelming"** refers to something that is too much to handle, overpowering, or very intense. (भारी)
 
 
• **Example:** The workload this week is overwhelming, and I don't know how I will complete it all on time.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that "bitten off more than you can chew" is an appropriate idiom to describe taking on overwhelming work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **At the eleventh hour** (अंतिम क्षणों में): Refers to something happening at the last possible moment.

 
 
• **Example:** They submitted their project at the eleventh hour, just before the deadline.
 
 
 
• **Called it a day** (काम समाप्त कर दिया): Means to stop working on something, especially for the day.
 
 
• **Example:** After working for 12 hours straight, she decided to call it a day.
 
 
 
• **Put something on ice** (किसी चीज़ को स्थगित करना): Means to postpone or delay something.
 
 
• **Example:** The company has decided to put the new project on ice due to budget constraints.
